beats.vo: Two men... walking... lifted six tons of marble into the sky.
This is the polyspastos. The Roman crane that built an empire.
And it hides a trick most people never see.
Look at the rope. It doesn't go up once... it goes up five times.
Every pass through a pulley splits the weight again.
Six thousand kilos... becomes twelve hundred.
Then comes the treadwheel. Four and a half meters wide.
A man walking inside it gains another thirty to one.
So fifty kilos of footsteps... becomes six thousand kilos of lift.
That is a hundred and twenty times stronger than a man pulling a rope.
Egypt needed ramps and thousands of workers. Rome needed two men... and a wheel.
And when Rome fell... Europe forgot how to build this. For a thousand years.
Which lost machine should I rebuild next? Comment A... or B.

metadata.description:
The Roman polyspastos: 5 pulleys + a 4.5 m treadwheel turned two men walking into 6,000 kg of lift — 120× stronger than a man pulling a rope. Then Europe forgot how to build it for 1,000 years.

3D reconstruction by Ancient Tech. Comment A or B to pick the next machine we rebuild.

Sources: Vitruvius, De Architectura X; Roman crane studies (Lancaster, O'Connor).
